===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:after|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|after}}, from {{inh|en|ang|æfter}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*aftar}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*after}}, {{m|gem-pro|*aftiri}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂epo|*h₂epoteros|t=further behind, further away}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂epo|t=off, away}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|efter|t=after}}, {{cog|frr|efter|t=after, behind}}, {{cog|fy|after}}, {{m|fy|achter}}, {{m|fy|efter|t=behind; after}}, {{cog|nds,nl|achter|t=behind}}, {{cog|de|after-|t=after-}}, {{cog|da,sv|efter|t=after}}, {{cog|nb,nn|etter|t=after}}, {{cog|fo,is|eftir|t=after}}.

The Irish usage to indicate recent completion of an activity is a calque of the Irish collocation {{m|ga|Táim [[tar éis]]...||I have just...|lit=I am after...}}.
